lead: The frame of one page of an app: a [PageHeader](#headerApi) (title, one line of description, actions on the right), the content, and a footer, with the padding and the space between them from the **theme style**. Every page of every app is framed the same way, because the theme decides how, not each project's CSS. It is the look only: the tab, the breadcrumb and the route stay in the app. Put the main action of a page in `actions` (one primary [Button](/button)), not in the toolbar of a table; put what finishes a page, such as Cancel and Save, in a `PageFooter`.

usage.title: Tickets
usage.description: Every request that became a ticket, newest first.
usage.content: The content of the page: cards, a table, a form.

actions.title: Customers
actions.description: The people who write to you, and the companies they work for.

fill.title: Tickets
fill.content: `fill` makes the page as high as the area it is in, and a Card with `fill` takes what is left: the table inside scrolls its rows under a fixed header.

levels.title: Heading level
levels.description: The title is an h3 by default. `level` sets the heading (h1–h5) and with it the size from the theme style's type scale; a page has one h1, so use `level={1}` where the header is the page's main heading.
levels.label: Heading level

styling.title: Styling Reference
styling.description: `page`, `page-body` and `page-footer` (the frame, its content and the bar at the bottom, with `data-fill`, `data-sticky` and `data-align`) are styled by `page.css`; `page-header`, `page-header-main` and `page-header-actions` by `page-header.css`. The title and the description are Title and Text.

states.title: Loading and not found
states.description: While a detail page's data loads, `loading` puts a spinner in place of the content; when the thing is not there, `notFound` (an `Empty`, a `Text`) does, and wins. The header and the frame stay, so the page looks the same in every state.
states.label: State
